title: add-kernel-lifecycle-sampler-and-perf-dashboard-annotations
author: Jordan Alvarez
description: Introduce a lightweight kernel lifecycle sampler and dashboard annotation hooks to improve visibility into per-kernel latency, queueing, and KV-cache interaction in the serving runtime. Motivation: production incidents in Oct/Nov showed transient latency spikes correlated with long tail kernel scheduling and cache thrash; existing NVTX ranges were useful but lacked compact per-kernel occupancy histograms and cross-request tag continuity. This PR adds: 1) a thread-local kernel lifecycle sampler that records kernel enqueue/start/complete timestamps with a compact ring buffer; 2) per-kernel occupancy counters exposed as exponentially-bucketed HDR-style histograms; 3) a small annotation API to emit short-lived dashboard events (start/stop markers) that are mapped to Grafana variables in the observability-pack; 4) KV-cache probe points to record soft-hit vs hard-miss latencies and a per-request hit-sequence fingerprint to aid regression triage; 5) lightweight continuous-batching probes that capture batch size distributions and per-batch scheduling delays. Implementation is runtime-only and conditioned behind a runtime flag (--enable-runtime-sampler) so cost-free when disabled. The description below documents usage, compatibility, and verification steps. Usage: enable flag on dedicated/private and hosted dev clusters; sampler outputs to /var/run/redwood/sampler.sock (unix socket) and integrates with existing observability-exporter via a new microprofile exporter that ships small JSON/line proto events. Backwards compatibility: the API is additive and feature-flag guarded; NVTX integration remains unchanged but now the sampler enriches NVTX ranges with kernel IDs for easier aggregation. Testing: unit tests for ring buffer semantics, integration test against perf-canary harness, and microbench added for 50/95/99 latency regression checks. Linked work: ENG-3284 (runtime observability), ENG-3340 (scheduling regressions).

review_comments: Asha: requested lowering syscall frequency and exposing an opt-in exporter; Miguel: asked for clearer semantics around ringbuffer overflow and suggested HDR bucketing; Claire: asked for a smaller surface area for hosted runtime and added flag gating. Author replies: implemented batching of exporter writes, added overflow drop counter with sampling, and moved default to disabled. Follow-up: add rollout notes to Dedicated runbook. Final: approved after microbench shows 0.5% median wall-time overhead in non-production sample and clear improvements in 99th percentile scheduling latency on perf-canary.
release_notes: Add runtime kernel lifecycle sampler and dashboard annotations (experimental, disabled by default); exposes KV-cache hit/miss probes; adds microbench for batch scheduling; configuration behind --enable-runtime-sampler flag; recommended for Debug/Canary deployments;
benchmark_results: perf-canary with sampler: 99p scheduling delay = 28ms (after tuning scheduler knobs)
microbench overhead: median +0.5%, p99 +1.2% when sampler enabled
testing: Unit tests: sampler ring buffer semantics and HDR helper; Integration: perf-canary runs with CI gating; E2E: deployed on internal dedicated cluster with flag enabled and exercised via continuous-batching workload; CI pipeline added to run microbench and report regression diffs.
notes_for_ops: Sampler writes to unix socket and exporter batches events; when enabling at scale, set exporter batch_size to >=128 and sampling_rate to 0.01 to bound metric cardinality. Add grafana dashboard variable sampler_scope to filter annotations per deployment. Follow rollout plan in docs/observability/runtime-sampler.md.
